text: That is not true, shouted the banker. <break time="0.8s" /> I bet you two million. <break time="0.8s" /> You could not stay in a prison cell. <break time="0.8s" /> For even five years. <break time="0.8s" /> If you mean it seriously. <break time="0.8s" /> Said the lawyer. <break time="0.8s" /> I will stay. <break time="0.8s" /> Not five, but fifteen years. <break time="0.8s" /> The bet was agreed. <break time="0.8s" /> And the banker. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had more millions. <break time="0.8s" /> Than he could count. <break time="0.8s" /> Was delighted. <break time="0.8s" /> Later that evening. <break time="0.8s" /> The banker began. <break time="0.8s" /> To think more seriously. <break time="0.8s" /> What is the point. <break time="0.8s" /> Of this bet. <break time="0.8s" /> What will it prove. <break time="0.8s" /> For me it was the foolishness of a rich man. <break time="0.8s" /> And for him it was simple greed for money. <break time="0.8s" /> It was decided that the lawyer would live alone. <break time="0.8s" /> In a small building. <break time="0.8s" /> In the bankers garden. <break time="0.8s" /> He could not see any people. <break time="0.8s" /> Hear human voices. <break time="0.8s" /> Or receive letters or newspapers. <break time="0.8s" /> But he could have books, music, and wine. <break time="0.8s" /> And he could ask for them. <break time="0.8s" /> By writing notes. <break time="0.8s" /> Through a small window. <break time="0.8s" /> If he left even two minutes early. <break time="0.8s" /> The banker would not have to pay. <break time="0.8s" /> Him anything.
